c1-10-001.gate_key: adv_can | C1 | mcq | Which sentence has a mistake? | Last night the children could stay up until eleven.

key.correct: Last night the children could stay up until eleven.
wrong: I could hear the neighbours arguing all night.
We couldn't go out on school nights.
In the end we were allowed to leave early.

item.q: Which sentence has a mistake?
item.why: Permission on one occasion: *were allowed to*, not *could*: *Last night the children were allowed to stay up until eleven.* *could* is for permission that was always there, and *couldn't* is fine for both.
item.why_lv: Atļauja vienā reizē: *were allowed to*, nevis *could*: *Last night the children were allowed to stay up until eleven.* *could* ir atļaujai, kas bija vienmēr, un *couldn't* der abos gadījumos.
item.correct: Last night the children could stay up until eleven.
wrong: I could hear the neighbours arguing all night.
We couldn't go out on school nights.
In the end we were allowed to leave early.

c1-10-002.gate_key: adv_can | C1 | mcq | Which sentence has a mistake? | May the figures in the report be wrong?

key.correct: May the figures in the report be wrong?
wrong: The results may point to a wider problem.
The trains might be late because of the snow.
Is she likely to accept the offer?

item.q: Which sentence has a mistake?
item.why: We don't ask about possibility with *May…?*: *Could the figures be wrong?* or *Are the figures likely to be wrong?*
item.why_lv: Par iespējamību nejautā ar *May*…?: *Could the figures be wrong?* vai *Are the figures likely to be wrong?*
item.correct: May the figures in the report be wrong?
wrong: The results may point to a wider problem.
The trains might be late because of the snow.
Is she likely to accept the offer?

c1-10-003.gate_key: adv_can | C1 | mcq | Which sentence has a mistake? | Nothing's on, so we might as good go to bed.

key.correct: Nothing's on, so we might as good go to bed.
wrong: You may well be right about the price.
You might have told me the café was closed.
There's no milk, so I'll have my tea black.

item.q: Which sentence has a mistake?
item.why: *might / may as well* (not *as good*) = it is the only sensible thing: *we might as well go to bed*.
item.why_lv: *might / may as well* (nevis *as good*) = tas ir vienīgais saprātīgais: *we might as well go to bed*.
item.correct: Nothing's on, so we might as good go to bed.
wrong: You may well be right about the price.
You might have told me the café was closed.
There's no milk, so I'll have my tea black.

item.why_lv: Iespējama darbība nākotnes brīdī: *may be + -ing, I may be lying on a beach*.

item.q: He didn't sound serious about leaving. He ___ ___ ___ ___.

item.why_lv: Iespējama darbība pagātnē: *might have been + -ing, he might have been joking*.

c1-10-007.gate_key: adv_can | C1 | mcq | Which sentence has a mistake? | Winters here are able to be very long.

item.q: Which sentence has a mistake?
item.why: *can* for what is sometimes or typically true, not *be able to*: *Winters here can be very long.*
item.why_lv: *can* tam, kas mēdz būt vai ir raksturīgi, nevis *be able to*: *Winters here can be very long.*
item.correct: Winters here are able to be very long.
wrong: Travelling with small children can be exhausting.

c1-10-008.gate_key: adv_can | C1 | mcq | Which sentence has a mistake? | Although she may be young, but she learns fast.

key.correct: Although she may be young, but she learns fast.
wrong: The flat may be small, but it's bright and quiet.
He might not be the fastest, but he never gives up.
It may well rain later, so take an umbrella.

item.q: Which sentence has a mistake?
item.why: *may … but* already admits one point and then disagrees, so *although* is not needed: *She may be young, but she learns fast.*
item.why_lv: *may* … *but* jau atzīst vienu un tad *iebilst*, tāpēc *although* nav vajadzīgs: *She may be young, but she learns fast.*
item.correct: Although she may be young, but she learns fast.
wrong: The flat may be small, but it's bright and quiet.
He might not be the fastest, but he never gives up.

answer_notes: Also possible, about a time in the past.
Arī pareizi, ja runa ir par laiku pagātnē.

c1-10-010.gate_key: adv_order | C1 | text | Start with *Had*: If I had known about the traffic, I would have left earlier. |

item.why: A condition without *if*: *Had* + subject + past participle: *Had I known…*
item.why_lv: Nosacījums bez *if*: *Had* + teikuma priekšmets + 3. forma: *Had I known*…
answers: Had I known about the traffic, I would have left earlier.
Had I known about the traffic, I'd have left earlier.
Had I known about the traffic, I would've left earlier.

c1-10-013.gate_key: adv_part | C1 | gap | Write one word in each gap: ___ ___ anyone in the city, he felt very lonely at first. (not / know) |

item.q: Write one word in each gap: ___ ___ anyone in the city, he felt very lonely at first. (not / know)
item.why: *Not* + *-ing* for a reason: *Not knowing anyone, he felt lonely.* *Not* goes first.
item.why_lv: *Not + -ing* iemeslam: *Not knowing anyone, he felt lonely.* *Not* stāv pirms formas ar *-ing*.

c1-10-014.gate_key: adv_past | C1 | gap | Write one word in each gap: The smoke alarm ___ off as soon as he ___ the candle underneath it. (go / light) |

item.q: Write one word in each gap: The smoke alarm ___ off as soon as he ___ the candle underneath it. (go / light)

item.why_lv: Divi pabeigti notikumi, kas seko viens otram: abiem Past Simple (*went off as soon as he lit*). Continuous forma nozīmētu, ka viens jau notika, kad notika otrs.

item.why_lv: *know* ir stāvokļa darbības vārds: Past Perfect Simple, *had known*, nevis *had been knowing*.

c1-10-017.gate_key: adv_perfect | C1 | gap | It's only eleven, and I ___ the bank four times. Nobody's answering. (ring) |

c1-10-023.gate_key: adv_present | C1 | gap | Write one word in each gap: So I'm at the bakery, I ___ ___ in the queue, and this woman suddenly ___ round and hands me her dog. (stand / turn) |

item.why: In a story told in the present, the background is in the present continuous (*I'm standing in the queue*) and the main events in the present simple (*turns, hands*).

c1-10-024.gate_key: adv_present | C1 | gap | Write one word in each gap: And Jones ___ the ball to Taylor, who ___ and scores! (pass / shoot) |

item.why_lv: Tiešraides komentārā ātras darbības, kas beidzas runāšanas brīdī, ir Present Simple: *passes, shoots, scores*. *is passing* aprakstītu ilgāku darbību, kas vēl notiek.
